title: Make the meter read 15 mA
story: A 9 V battery feeds node a through a 100 ohm sense resistor R0, so the current in R0 is everything the battery delivers. From node a, a 1 kohm resistor R1 already goes to ground. Add a second branch from a to ground so the total current through R0 lands between 14 and 16 mA. Every milliamp arriving at a must leave through R1 or your new branch.

goals.label: current through R0 (the battery current) between 14 and 16 mA
the new resistor stays under 1/4 W

hints: With only R1 in place, about 9 V / 1100 ohm = 8.2 mA flows. Your branch must add the rest.
KCL at node a: current in R0 = current in R1 + current in your resistor.
Node a sits about 1.5 V below the battery when 15 mA flows through R0, because 0.015 A x 100 ohm = 1.5 V.
